label: JZ Mock D · Paper 1 · Question 1
source: JZ Mock D · Paper 1 · Question 1 · Publisher worked solution
knowledgePattern: Collect every bracket selection with the target total power

hints.title: Choose terms that make the right power
hints.body: Think of the expression as five identical brackets. From each bracket you choose 2, −x or x2/2. Write the different ways those choices can give x4.
hints.recap: The powers of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> add when you multiply terms.
hints.pitfall: You must choose one term from each of the five brackets.
hints.pause: List how many <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> terms and how many <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> terms you use in each case.

recall.reminder: The powers of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> add when you multiply terms.

hints.title: Count the bracket choices
hints.body: For each case, choose which brackets supply x2/2, then which of the remaining brackets supply −x. The other brackets supply 2.
hints.recap: A binomial coefficient counts which brackets supply a chosen term.
hints.pitfall: Include the factors <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>, as well as the minus signs.
hints.pause: Calculate each contribution to the coefficient, then add them.

recall.reminder: A binomial coefficient counts which brackets supply a chosen term.

solution:
1. List the choices that give x4. Each of the five brackets contributes 2, −x or x2/2. We need either four copies of −x; two copies of −x and one of x2/2; or two copies of x2/2. Fill the remaining brackets with 2.

2. Count each contribution. Four copies of −x contribute (54)2=10 to the coefficient. For two copies of −x and one of x2/2, first choose the quadratic bracket and then the two linear brackets: the contribution is 5(42)(1/2)22=60. Finally, two quadratic brackets contribute (52)(1/2)223=20. All powers of the negative term are even.

3. Add the contributions. The coefficient is 10+60+20=90. Answer E.
